title: Room Six
intro: A guest book that knows who is coming. The lantern is lit.
body: I work the night desk at the Wayside Motel, out on Route 9, where the road runs between two towns that don't talk to each other. Twelve rooms. Most nights, nobody comes. The guest book sits open on the counter. The owner, Mr. Pell, likes ink. He says a name in ink is a promise. Every morning, when I hand over the keys, there's a new line in it. Room six. Signed at two fourteen a.m. A different name every night. Room six has been boarded up since before I was hired. The first week, I blamed the day staff. The second week, I stopped blaming anyone. I started watching. Last night, at two thirteen, the lights in the parking lot flickered. At two fourteen, the pen moved. Not much. Just a roll. Like someone had brushed it with a sleeve. I didn't look at the book. I looked at the camera. On the screen, I was sitting at the desk. And behind me, close enough to breathe on my neck, a man in a wet raincoat was leaning over my shoulder to write. I didn't turn around. I couldn't. When the lights came back, the office was empty. The book was open. The ink was still wet. Room six. Two fourteen a.m. And the name was mine. Mr. Pell came in at six. He read the line very quietly. Then he took a key off the hook. A key I had never seen. "It's always the one at the desk," he said. "Your room's ready."
outro: The Wayside Motel is still open. The night desk is always staffed. And if you sign the book, check the name above yours.
